name: Synchronization.Mutex (Swift 6)
baseline: NSLock, or an actor used as a lock
verdict_reason: The only published Swift numbers come from a debug build on a pre-release toolchain: Mutex was 1.6x faster than NSLock and 7.3x faster than an actor under 10-task contention. The direction is plausible because Mutex wraps os_unfair_lock on Apple platforms, but no release-build comparison was found.
tier_reason: Independent forum benchmark with code, Mac model and Xcode version posted, but run as a debug build on a pre-release toolchain.
claimed_speedup: 1.6x faster than NSLock (0.971 s vs 1.555 s) and 7.3x faster than an actor (0.971 s vs 7.098 s) for 10 tasks x 1_000_000 enqueues (derived from page data); in the same thread another poster measured an actor at ~50 s vs NSLock at ~2 s for 100M contended increments
workload: 10 child tasks in a TaskGroup, each enqueuing 1,000,000 Ints into one shared FIFO guarded by NSLock, Mutex, or an actor; wall-clock seconds for the whole group
toolchain: Xcode 15.2 with the swift-PR-71383-1223 pre-release toolchain; debug build
platforms: iOS 18+, macOS 15+, tvOS 18+, watchOS 11+, visionOS 2+, Linux, Windows
install: built into the Swift 6 standard library (import Synchronization); needs an iOS 18 / macOS 15 deployment target on Apple platforms
one_liner: Swift 6's cross-platform lock; 1.6x faster than NSLock and 7.3x faster than an actor in one debug-build test.
how_it_is_fast: Mutex stores the protected value inline and is noncopyable, so it has a stable address without a separate heap allocation. On Apple platforms it is built on os_unfair_lock, which takes the lock with an atomic compare-and-swap and only enters the kernel on contention. An actor used as a lock pays for task suspension and executor hops on every access.
use_it_when: Guarding small shared state that synchronous code also touches
Low-level data structures (queues, caches) where a hop to an actor per operation is too expensive
Code that must build on Linux and Windows as well as Apple platforms
skip_it_when: Deployment targets below iOS 18 / macOS 15 (use OSAllocatedUnfairLock or a backport such as swhitty/swift-mutex)
Long-running or blocking work inside the critical section; an actor suspends instead of blocking a thread
caveats: Debug build, so absolute times and possibly ratios differ from release builds
Pre-release toolchain from before Swift 6 shipped
Single run per variant, measured with Date(); no variance reported
The ~50 s actor and ~2 s NSLock figures come from a different poster whose build settings and hardware are not stated
tradeoffs: Not recursive; relocking on the same thread deadlocks
Blocks the calling thread under contention instead of suspending the task
Noncopyable type: it has to live in a class, global, or other stable storage
